d_dispatch.title: Dispatcher's Note
d_dispatch.text:
BLACKMOOR SIDING - 14 NOV

To whoever finds her under steam:

Train 13, the Vesper, is not on any timetable. The Hollowgate line was struck off in 1961. I have worked this yard thirty years and I have seen her come in on this night four times, cold and empty, lamps burning.

She will not stay. If you are aboard when she goes, keep her fed and keep her lights on. The things on this line do not like the light, and they do not like the whistle.

Fuel is in the cargo car. The firebox is in the cab. Do not pass a red signal. They did, once.

- H. Aldous, dispatcher

d_ticket.title: Punched Ticket
d_ticket.text:
NORTHERN VALE RAILWAY
Third class - single

BLACKMOOR to HOLLOWGATE
Train 13 'The Vesper'
14 November 1961

The ticket has been punched forty-six times.

d_telegram.title: Company Telegram
d_telegram.text:
TO STATION MASTER RAVENWOOD
14 NOV 1961 21.40

DISREGARD FAULT REPORT HOLLOWGATE TUNNEL STOP
LINE TO REMAIN OPEN UNTIL INSPECTION 16 NOV STOP
TRAIN 13 TO PROCEED ON SCHEDULE STOP
CLEAR YOUR SIGNAL STOP

DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS NVR

d_logbook.title: Station Master's Log
d_logbook.text:
14 Nov. 21.52 - Vesper arrived 4 min late. 46 passengers, conductor E. Crane.

21.55 - I held her at red. The tunnel men rang at dusk: water in the crown, timbers moving. Telegram from head office says clear the signal.

22.03 - Crane came to the box himself. Said the passengers were cold and wanted their beds. I told him what the tunnel men said. He laughed and said he had promised them Hollowgate by midnight.

22.07 - God forgive me. I pulled the lever. Green.

15 Nov. - Vesper not arrived Hollowgate. No word. The company men came and took the telegram book. They missed this one.

16 Nov. - The signal will not go back to red. I have cut the power to it.

d_guard.title: Trackwalker's Note
d_guard.text:
To the relief man,

I have taken the switch to pieces. Lever is with the search party at their camp north of the line, the rod is locked in here with me. Nothing more goes down to Hollowgate while I draw pay.

Do not walk the wood after dark. There is something thin that goes between the trees. It stands and looks. Shine a lamp on it and it backs away, but run and it hears you, and then it is quick.

If you must restore the switch you will want a wrench.

d_camp.title: Search Party Diary
d_camp.text:
Day 3. Eleven of us came up from Ravenwood to look for the Vesper. The company says she was never here.

Day 5. We found the tunnel mouth. A gate across it, new iron, welds still bright. Who gates a tunnel with a train inside?

Day 6. Porter did not come back from the stream. Something was standing where he had been. Tall. Arms too long.

Day 8. Four of us left. We hear the whistle at night, far under the hill. It sounds like it is asking for something.

Day 9. I am leaving the switch lever here. If you are reading this, do not go looking for us. Some of us are still walking.

d_shop.title: Shopkeeper's Ledger
d_shop.text:
Nov 20 - Sold: lamp oil, 9 tins. Everyone wants light.

Nov 23 - The Harrow family gone in the night. Table still laid.

Nov 27 - Conductor seen on the lane again. Old Crane, who went with the Vesper. He walks house to house and looks in at the windows as if he is counting.

Dec 1 - Wireless plays nothing but a man reading numbers. Inspector Voss has locked himself in the cellar under the workshop with his papers. He says the numbers are the lock.

Dec 2 - Closing the shop. Nobody left to sell to.

d_confession.title: Inspector's Confession
d_confession.text:
I, Tobias Voss, inspector of works, Northern Vale Railway, write this of my own will.

The Hollowgate tunnel was condemned in my report of October 1961. The Director struck out the page. A closed tunnel pays no dividend.

On 14 November the crown came down behind train 13. Not on her. Behind her. She was sealed in the hill with forty-six passengers, a crew of three, and air for perhaps two days.

We could have dug. The Director ordered a gate welded across the mouth and the line removed from the maps. No train, no tunnel, no inquiry.

They were alive in there when we gated it. I heard the whistle.

She comes back every year on the night. She is still trying to finish the route. I think she will keep coming until someone takes her through.

d_gate.title: Works Order 1961/114
d_gate.text:
NORTHERN VALE RAILWAY - WORKS DEPT

Hollowgate tunnel, east portal.

1. Erect steel gate across running line. Weld shut.
2. Remove valve wheel and winch gear from gate mechanism. Store separately.
3. Disconnect portal generator. Remove fuses.
4. Junction beyond gate: leave set for SERVICE BYPASS. Nothing is to be routed to Hollowgate platform.
5. No record of this order is to be kept.

A pencil note underneath: 'Then why is the platform lamp still lit?'

d_truth.title: Passenger Manifest - Train 13
d_truth.text:
THE VESPER - 14 NOVEMBER 1961
Blackmoor to Hollowgate. 46 passengers.

The pages list every name, seat by seat. Families. A doctor. Two soldiers going home. A child travelling alone, seat 31.

The last page is in a different hand:

'Day 2 in the dark. I promised them Hollowgate. A conductor delivers his passengers. I have told them to stay seated. I will walk the train until we arrive.

If you hold this, you know their names. That is all a manifest is for: to say who is aboard, and to be signed when they are delivered.

Take us to the platform. Read the names. Let them get off.

Do not take the bypass. The bypass is how the living leave. It is not how the dead arrive.

- E. Crane, conductor'
